claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The unmodified alloy suffers from cracking and poor mechanical integrity.
Adding approximately 5 wt% of a finely dispersed Cu-rich metallic binder will improve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
The proposed binder is ductile and rare-earth-free.
The binder will form an interpenetrating microstructure.
The binder will preferentially locate at grain boundaries and crack-initiation sites.
Binder localization at grain boundaries and crack-initiation sites will redistribute applied stress.
The ductile binder will act as an intrinsic crack arrester.
The binder will enhance load transfer and homogenize stress.
A 5 wt% binder addition will leave most of the caloric parent phase intact.
Retaining most of the parent phase will keep its field-induced entropy changes largely unaltered.
The binder-containing material will have at least 20% greater compressive strength than the unmodified alloy.
The binder-containing material is expected to attain a compressive strength near or above 152 MPa.
The binder-containing material will exhibit less than a 5% reduction in caloric effect relative to the unmodified alloy.
The predicted mechanical and caloric outcomes will persist under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The predicted outcomes will persist during cyclic temperature and mechanical loading typical of the intended application.

contradictions.description: The conditions require cyclic temperature loading while also stating that all testing occurs at room temperature. A temperature-cycle range around room temperature is not supplied, so these boundary statements are internally ambiguous and potentially incompatible.
